geographic_scope.district_scope: A source is district-applicable only when the source explicitly identifies that district. Named study locations are not silently converted to district claims.

status_definitions.source_verified: The cited source was directly accessible and its cited bibliographic/content details were checked. This is not agronomic approval.
status_definitions.source_unverified: The source could not be independently accessed or its claim could not be verified.
status_definitions.expert_review_required: The source is accessible, but local applicability, interpretation or operational use needs qualified review.
status_definitions.expert_approved: A named agricultural reviewer has approved the evidence and its stated scope.
status_definitions.conflicting_evidence: Accessible sources disagree on a claim; neither claim is silently selected.
status_definitions.insufficient_evidence: No verified, applicable evidence was found for this crop-stage-concern combination.

general_guidance.crop_stage: Zone- and condition-specific varietal selection; late nursery transplanting and late planting are named
general_guidance.institution: Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR), New Delhi
general_guidance.source_section: Andhra Pradesh paddy varieties by zone and crop/planting condition
general_guidance.source_fact: The ICAR Andhra Pradesh section lists paddy varieties by named zones and separately addresses scarce-rainfall/drought-prone, flood-prone, saline-soil and brown-planthopper-prone contexts, late nursery transplanting and late planting.
general_guidance.limitations: The publication does not map its recommendations to every district. Confirm current local suitability with an agricultural officer. This 2025 Kharif publication is not a current-season advisory and is not evidence for a FarmShield risk threshold.

general_guidance.crop_stage: Boot-leaf or 'lowering' stage (source wording; not mapped to FarmShield stages)
general_guidance.institution: Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR), New Delhi
general_guidance.source_section: Andhra Pradesh, Precautions during natural calamities
general_guidance.source_fact: The source reports that submergence for more than 1 to 2 days at the named stages may impair panicle exertion; water accumulation in spikelets may reduce fertilisation and lead to chaffy seeds.
general_guidance.limitations: The source wording is retained and is not mapped to FarmShield's growth-stage taxonomy. This duration is not a validated risk threshold or forecast rule. The guidance is not district-specific and needs local expert review.

general_guidance.institution: Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR), New Delhi
general_guidance.source_section: Andhra Pradesh paddy, Fertilizer Application section (preceding green-manure crops only)
general_guidance.source_fact: The source names Dhaincha, Sunhemp, Pillipesara and Cowpea as green-manure crops to grow before paddy.
general_guidance.limitations: Only the preceding-crop statement is included; fertilizer rates and prescriptions are intentionally excluded. The publication does not establish district-specific applicability.

general_guidance.institution: Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR), New Delhi
general_guidance.source_section: Andhra Pradesh paddy, Bacterial leaf blight entry (non-chemical statements only)
general_guidance.source_fact: Under its bacterial leaf blight entry, ICAR says affected stubbles may be destroyed by ploughing and advises against clipping seedling tips during transplanting.
general_guidance.limitations: This records practices listed under a disease heading; it does not diagnose a crop or establish treatment effectiveness. Chemical and fertilizer directions are omitted. Confirm disease identification and local applicability with a qualified agricultural officer.

general_guidance.institution: Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR), New Delhi
general_guidance.source_section: Andhra Pradesh paddy, Trap Barrier System (TBS)
general_guidance.source_fact: The source describes a trap-barrier system erected around the crop 15 days after transplanting and says traps should be checked daily and emptied or replaced.
general_guidance.limitations: The publication does not map this practice to specific districts in the cited passage. Its timing is a source practice, not a weather-risk threshold. Confirm suitability and safe installation locally.

general_guidance.source_title: Package of practices (PoP’s)of groundnut for different states
general_guidance.publication_date: 2018 (PDF creation metadata and upload path; publication year not printed)
general_guidance.page_reference: PDF pp.1, 3 (Andhra Pradesh sowing time; crop duration and harvest)
general_guidance.source_section: Andhra Pradesh: Sowing time; Crop duration; Harvesting
general_guidance.source_fact: The Andhra Pradesh section lists Kharif sowing from 15 June to 31 July and Rabi sowing in November–December. It gives crop durations of 100–110 days for Kharif and 110–120 days for Rabi and says harvest is done after 80% of pods mature.
general_guidance.limitations: The document does not print a publication year; 2018 is inferred only from PDF creation metadata and the URL upload path. This older state-level reference is not district-specific or a current local calendar. Its dates and maturity description are not FarmShield risk thresholds.

general_guidance.source_title: Package of practices (PoP’s)of groundnut for different states
general_guidance.publication_date: 2018 (PDF creation metadata and upload path; publication year not printed)
general_guidance.source_fact: The source lists Spanish types Kadiri-6, Narayani, ICGV-91114, Kadiri-9, Harithandhra, Anantha, Dharani, TAG-24, Greeshma, Tirupati-4, Kadiri Amaravathi and Kadiri Chitrvathi, and Virginia type Kadiri 7 Bold, under Andhra Pradesh.
general_guidance.limitations: This is a historical list, not a current cultivar endorsement or a district-level recommendation. Confirm seed availability and local suitability with a qualified agricultural officer.

general_guidance.source_title: Package of practices (PoP’s)of groundnut for different states
general_guidance.publication_date: 2018 (PDF creation metadata and upload path; publication year not printed)
general_guidance.source_fact: The source states that manure and fertilizer use must follow soil-test-based recommendations and mentions organic amendments and biofertilizer practices.
general_guidance.limitations: Numerical fertilizer, amendment and seed-treatment doses are intentionally omitted. This older state-level source does not establish a personalized recommendation; base nutrient decisions on current soil tests and qualified local advice.

general_guidance.crop_stage: Flowering, peg penetration (pegging), and pod development
general_guidance.source_title: Package of practices (PoP’s)of groundnut for different states
general_guidance.publication_date: 2018 (PDF creation metadata and upload path; publication year not printed)
general_guidance.source_section: Andhra Pradesh: Irrigation management; soil-moisture conservation
general_guidance.source_fact: The source identifies flowering, peg penetration and pod development as critical irrigation stages. It describes an irrigated schedule of eight to nine irrigations at ten-day intervals, with the last at 90–95 days after sowing, and rainfed soil-moisture conservation using groundnut-shell mulch.
general_guidance.limitations: These are practices reported by an older source, not a weather trigger or personalized schedule. Soil, rainfall, cultivar, water availability and current local recommendations affect suitability; the source does not identify Guntur-specific conditions.

general_guidance.source_title: Package of practices (PoP’s)of groundnut for different states
general_guidance.publication_date: 2018 (PDF creation metadata and upload path; publication year not printed)
general_guidance.source_section: Andhra Pradesh: Weed management; intercropping; foliar-disease and field-hygiene entries
general_guidance.source_fact: Among its non-chemical practices, the source describes inter-cultivation and hand-weeding, intercrops and border or trap crops, removing Parthenium before flowering, and destroying plants identified in the source as PBND-infected.
general_guidance.limitations: Chemical pest-control and herbicide prescriptions are excluded. The source does not validate diagnosis, treatment effectiveness or district-level suitability; do not identify disease from this general reference alone.
